questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a claim about a mapping technique
questions.stem: Note CP-557 claims using a polar projection proves Arctic detail is exact.

answer.exemplar: A polar projection improves polar representation but does not alone prove exactness; survey data and method must also be checked.

questions.explanation: A polar projection improves polar representation but does not alone prove exactness. Survey data and method matter.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Recognize an argument that escapes refutation

stimulus.body: Note CP-558 defends a graticule by saying any irregularity is due to Earth's shape.

questions.stem: In note CP-558, what is the logical weakness?

options.text: Blaming Earth's shape for any irregularity makes the claim untestable.

questions.explanation: Attributing every irregularity to Earth's shape makes the graticule claim unfalsifiable. A testable tolerance is needed.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish between competing causes

stimulus.body: Note CP-559 attributes a color shift to aging, ignoring possible lighting differences. No comparison is given.

questions.stem: Stage 1: What is the core flaw in note CP-559?

options.text: It proves aging caused the shift.
It picks one cause while ignoring a rival explanation.

questions.explanation: Attributing the shift to aging while ignoring lighting skips a rival cause. Both should be compared.

questions.stem: Stage 1: Note CP-560 claims a new font caused fewer errors because errors fell after adoption.
